title: The three charts — #277, rebuilt
headline: Three decisions, and what they cost.

decisions.title: Land the {obeys_total} authored citations now, or read them first?
decisions.lede: Filename join on the three data-visualisation-*-charts.md files: {n_line_file} line rules, {n_pie_file} pie rules, {n_bar_file} bar rules — {n_spec_total} in all. {obeys_total} bind and carry one authored sentence each; {drops_total} do not bind and are declared drops, named in Part A below. The two options differ in one thing only: whether you read the {obeys_total} sentences before they land or after.
options: Land now. The three metas go into knowledge/components/ exactly as they sit in proposed-metas/ — one spliced span each. You would be landing {obeys_total} sentences you have not read; Part A prints all {obeys_total} of them plus the {drops_total} drop reasons, so "not read" is your choice, not a shortage of material.

Land after a per-component read. Nothing lands this wave. You read chart-line, then chart-pie, then chart-bar — {obeys_total} sentences and {drops_total} drop reasons, one chart at a time — and what survives lands in the following lane.
decisions.why: Two seats read the same four files independently and reached the same {drops_total} drops by the same reasoning — dv-line-009 and dv-line-010 are the spark's rules sitting in the line's file, and dv-pie-003 is the doughnut-centre rule in a file whose namesake has no centre. That convergence is the strongest signal either lane produced, and it is an argument for (a).
decisions.attrib: Lane CO proposed the citations; lane CJ reached the same three drops independently; lane CV re-drove both.

decisions.title: Does chart-donut share the pie file?
decisions.lede: The precedent is icon-button, which takes {icon_button_n} of the buttons spec's {ctk_buttons} rules because that spec names icon-only as one of its three structural variations. The pie file names the doughnut harder than that: its Types section lists Doughnut as one of two types, dv-pie-009's normative text reads "both pie and doughnut", and dv-pie-003 binds the donut alone. Measured the other way, the provenance runs backwards: chart-pie.meta.json says it was ported from Chart-donut.reference.html with the inner radius dropped to 0, and chart-donut.meta.json already cites dv-pie-009 and dv-pie-010 by id in its own antiPatterns. There is no family edge between them — {family_edges} of {metas_total} metas carry one and neither chart does; what exists is chart-pie's not-with and yieldsTo pointing at chart-donut.
options: Yes — chart-donut takes the pie file as its home spec, all {n_pie_file} rules including dv-pie-003. Authored in a following lane, same shape as this one. Cost: +{n_pie_file} obeys edges on top of whatever D-1 and D-3 land.

No — chart-donut waits. The filename does not say donut, and admitting it on prose is a step toward the tier s276-D5 refused. ⚠ Choosing this strands dv-pie-003: chart-pie drops it as donut-only and nothing else takes it, so an ingested rule ends the wave governing no component at all — a visible zero created by us, not found by us.
decisions.why: Yes — chart-donut takes data-visualisation-pie-charts.md as its home spec because the file itself names the doughnut as one of its two types, so author all {n_pie_file} pie rules on the donut and only {pie_n} on the pie: dv-pie-003 binds the donut alone and stays off chart-pie.
decisions.attrib: Lane CJ's recommendation, its words. Lane CO reached the same reading from the other side and declined to rule it.

decisions.title: Where do the {dv_family} family rules in data-visualisation.md attach?
decisions.lede: They sit above all three, and the corpus's answer today is nowhere: common-toolkit-foundations.md holds {ctk_foundations} rules above the four components lane TO authored and 0 are attached to any meta. So there is no precedent to follow, only one to set. Two blind lanes read all {dv_family} against all three and agreed on {agreed_rules} of {dv_family}. Of the {n_cells} cells in that matrix they agreed on {agreed_cells}; three disagreed; a third lane measured two of the three against the files and settled them. The reconciled figure is {family_b_total}.
options: Attach all {dv_family} to each of the three — {family_a_total} edges. Simple, and {family_false} of them would be false, each carrying an authored-looking sentence. That is the s274-D12 shape wearing a sentence.

Attach the authored subset per component — {family_b_total} edges: {family_bar} on bar, {family_line} on line, {family_pie} on pie. Each read against that chart. {family_shared} of the {dv_family} bind all three identically, which is the first measurement of what a family node would have to carry.

Attach them to a chart family node instead — {family_family_total} edges once. Nothing can carry it today: obeys lives on component metas, role:chart-panel has the wrong membership ({role_members} members, and Chart-bullet is not one), and it would need a new node kind, an inheritance edge type and a propagation rule — three vocabulary changes, each yours.
decisions.why: Option (b), at {family_b_total}. Lane CO measured {co_total} and lane CJ measured {cj_total}; both were arithmetically correct against their own matrix, and the gap is three cells, not a sum. Two are settled on the files — dv-008 does bind the pie, and dv-015 binds the role rather than the line. One is yours, below.
decisions.attrib: Lane CJ recommended (b) at {cj_total}; lane CO measured {co_total}; lane CV reconciled the two matrices cell by cell to {family_b_total}. All three recommend (b).
